text:
amanda: Heads up — noticed a p99 regression in the Llama3-13B canary around token ~70. Looks like a kernel switch + KV churn. attaching quick snippets below :eyes:

kai: Ugh, that pattern again. Is it the auto kernel selector falling back to fp16 mid-sequence?

amanda: Yeah exactly. Bench logs show `fast_gemm_int4` used for tokens 0..69 then fallback to `fallback_gemm_fp16` at 70 and p99 jumps. KV evict rate spikes concurrently.

ravi: Could be affinity/stride mismatch with int4 tiled kernels + our KV layout. Did you enable quantized prefetch?

amanda: We did. Config used for the canary: 
```
model: llama-3-13b
hidden_size: 5120
head_dim: 128
num_heads: 40
rope_theta: 1.02
quant: int4-fused
kernel_selection: auto
batching: continuous
max_batch_tokens: 2048
prefetch: true
```

julia: Also note chat template: we add a repeating system chunk which doubles the prefix length for certain requests — that can push the token index into a different kernel path.

perf-bot: perf report attached: stable-run 2026-03-05T12:34Z
```
summary:
  median: 142ms
  p95: 268ms
  p99: 520ms  # spike at token 71
kernel_usage:
  0-69: fast_gemm_int4 (avg 120ms)
  70+: fallback_gemm_fp16 (avg 430ms)
kv_metrics:
  evicts_per_min: 32 -> 98 at spike
  cache_hit_ratio: 0.87 -> 0.61
batch_fill: 3/8 -> 7/8 (more batching but slower kernel)
```

amanda: Repro command I used: `./bench_local --model llama-3-13b --seq 128 --prefill 64 --quant int4-fused --profile`

kai: Two immediate hypotheses: (1) int4 kernel is brittle for head_dim 128 when rope_theta != default and kernel selector heuristics flip mid-episode; (2) KV page alignment causes the int4 tiled kernel to miss and force fallback.

ravi: I can run a microprobe to toggle kernel selection and force `prefer_fp16` and `force_int4` to compare. Also will add a KV alignment check (stride % tile == 0).

julia: Small experiment: change rope_theta to 0.99 (we've seen drift from 1.02 cause attention weight distribution shift) — might keep the fast kernel stable. Worth trying before we change batching heuristics.

amanda: Good call. Can we also try reducing `max_batch_tokens` to avoid hit thresholds that trigger different kernel path?

perf-bot: queued job 3778881234-1: microprobe-kernel-override (ravi). ETA ~ 18m.

ravi: Running two probes now:
- probe A: kernel_selection=force_int4, prefetch=true, kv_align_check=on
- probe B: kernel_selection=prefer_fp16, prefetch=true, kv_align_check=on
Should have results in ~12m.

kai: If probe A still thrashed, let's instrument the selector with a simple predicate: `if token_index > 64 and batch_fill > .6 then prefer_fp16` — temporary guard to avoid mid-sequence fallback.

amanda: Can we also capture a short NVTX trace? Want to see where time is spent inside the kernel.

ravi: NVTX attached to both probes. Early look: probe A shows kernel entry times aligned but memory copy waits spike at 70. probe B avoids fallback path and p99 drops to 210ms.

amanda: Nice. So forcing fp16 avoids the thrash; tradeoff is higher median for int4 path in some cases but avoids cliff.

julia: Action items:
- ravi: finish microprobe, post full logs + NVTX (assigned)
- kai: add temporary selector predicate to avoid mid-sequence flips (canary knob)
- amanda: prepare canary with rope_theta tweak and reduced max_batch_tokens to see if we can keep int4 stable without resorting to fp16

ravi: Posted probe artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/probes/3778881234/{probeA,probeB}/. nvtx.tar.gz included.

amanda: Thanks. Also adding a short note: watch for chat-template induced duplicate system tokens — preprocessing should dedupe identical adjacent system messages to avoid unnecessary prefix growth.

kai: Agreed. I'll open a tiny PR to dedupe system prefix and add the selector guard.

amanda: 👍 Will follow up with canary results tomorrow.

perf-bot: reminder: if we keep `force_fp16` as interim, add a ticket to evaluate unit-cost impact across traffic samples (per-token cost vs p99 SLA). :chart_with_upwards_trend:

ravi: logged PERF-1729 with artifacts and recommended next steps.

julia: One more datapoint — Mistral/mixtral seemed less sensitive to this pattern because their head_dim alignments map better to int4 tiles. Might help prioritize model-specific kernel affinity rules.

amanda: Great — let's table model-specific affinity table (head_dim -> preferred kernel) as a medium-term work item.

kai: OK, closing this thread for now. Reopen if spike reappears after fixes. :lock:
